provenance.wordSourceNote: Batch 29's remainingA1Gap note grouped the leftover words into 4 buckets (adverbs 19, pronouns 13, dependent nouns 13, determiners 11) without separating numerals/interjections. Re-auditing the raw NIKL CSV by homograph: the 'determiners 11' bucket bundles 3 true 관형사 (무슨/어떤/여러) with 8 numeral/determiner homograph pairs (마흔/백만/서른/십만/아흔/억/여든/일흔, each tagged BOTH 관형사 and 수사 for the same string) that this batch treats as numbers (counter-swap technique, pos_de=Nomen matching how 백/천/만/이십.../칠십 are already tagged live) rather than true determiners (pos_de=Adjektiv, matching 새/다른/모든/몇 precedent). 억 is one of those 8 -- assigned to the live pack a1_numbers_2 (filling its order-4 gap, 11->12 words) rather than to the new a1_determiners_1 pack, since it is a numeral/determiner homograph, not a distinct extra word. The remaining pure numerals (구십/스물/팔십, no 관형사 homograph) and 2 interjections (그래/아) were not enumerated as separate buckets in Batch 29's prose note but are present in the raw NIKL CSV; this batch authors all of them. R8 (2026-09-16) added a 4th numeral, 천, that the initial word-list assembly had overlooked (see provenance.cheonDecisionNote) -- it was never actually excluded from the grade-1 gap list, only its old example sentence was deleted in an unrelated commit. 19+13+13+11(incl. 억)+4+2 = 62.

provenance.r8Revision: 2026-09-16 Fable coordinator review of commit d6b0c430, 3-point R8: (1) Connective adverbs (그래서/그러니까/그러면/그럼/그런데/그렇지만/그리고/하지만) switched from cross-cluster Tier A to Tier B (bare dictionary-form verb or bare particle) -- a sentence-initial connective slot accepts almost any OTHER connective too ('저는 배가 아파요. 그런데/그리고 병원에 가요.' both still read as valid Korean), so the cross-cluster swaps were D7 violations, not genuine nonsense. 그러면/그럼 additionally needed a question-then-response frame (a bare declarative doesn't felicitously open with either) with a named persona as the addressee, giving 2 of this batch's 4 true persona rows. (2) 천 added (60->61 core words, 62 with the 억 supplement) -- see cheonDecisionNote; 판정 필요 1 (억 vs 천) is now resolved as BOTH. (3) Persona rows tightened to the 'true speaker with an explicit marker' standard (vocative or an unambiguous first-person self-identification) -- the previous draft's 9 generic '저는...' attributions were not markers and are dropped; the function-word-batch floor is >=4 (not the >=8 used for verb/noun batches), met exactly by 마야(씨 counter row)/준(states his own name)/민호,레나(그러면/그럼 vocatives).

provenance.d6RedistributionNote: C3-T5b (2026-09-16, Fable brief + correction): D6 per-batch reuse cap -- a distractor WORD as the learner sees it (its whole particle tail stripped: 에서|에게|한테|으로|부터|까지|처럼|보다|하고|이랑|이나|에는|에서는|에게는|들+particle|을|를|이|가|은|는|에|로|도|과|와|만|랑|께|나, never cut below 2 syllables; Tier-B bare particles by surface form) may appear at most 4x within the batch -- enforced on the promoted cloze set. Before: 언제 7, 무엇 5. Changed distractors (draft and live assets/data/cloze.json kept identical): cloze_a1_0732 언제는/무엇은 -> 얼마는/뭐는 (quantity/thing class vs the person answer 그는; 0732 is a non-waived pronoun row judged by D3 same-ending, so any NIKL grade-1 question word with the topic particle qualifies), cloze_a1_0740 언제는 -> 그는 (OPEN_SLOT_WAIVER row: distractors must stay inside distractor_rules.PRONOUN_FOLD_CATEGORY_MISMATCHES, and 그는 is the only pool member not already at its cap -- same person-in-thing-slot category violation as cloze_a1_0742's approved 그는), cloze_a1_0743 언제에 -> 누구에 (person + locative 에 without 에게, a particle-form 비문). After: every word <= 4 (언제 4, 무엇 4, 어디 4). The 으로/로 fold rows (0734/0741) are unchanged: their only cap-compliant pool is exactly the three words they already use. Copula folds (언제예요/무엇이에요/어디예요) are NOT treated as particles here (they are not in the inventory); folding them would put 언제 at 6 / 무엇 5 / 어디 5, unreachable without widening the shared PRONOUN_FOLD pool -- flagged to Fable, not acted on. Sentence text untouched; asserted by test_batch_30_draft.py's test_no_distractor_stem_reused_more_than_4_times_within_batch.

posRules.adverbs_connective: R8 (2026-09-16): 8 discourse connectives (그래서/그러니까/그러면/그런데/그럼/그렇지만/그리고/하지만) use TIER B, not cross-cluster Tier A -- a first draft grouped them into 4 semantic clusters (result/conditional-then/contrast/additive) and drew distractors from a different cluster, but Fable's review found a sentence-initial connective slot accepts almost any OTHER connective too ('저는 배가 아파요. 그런데/그리고 병원에 가요.' both still read as valid Korean, just a different nuance) -- a D7 violation, not genuine nonsense. Distractors are now a bare dictionary-form verb or a bare grammatical particle (2+1 or 3+0, mirroring the PREDICATE_SLOT_WAIVER composition), tagged 'open connective frame': a bare verb/particle cannot open a second sentence as a connector at all, always 비문. 그러면/그럼 (the 2 response-type connectives) also needed their example restructured into a question-then-response frame ('민호 씨, 배가 고파요? 그러면 같이 밥을 먹어요.' / '레나 씨, 오늘 바빠요? 그럼 내일 만나요.') since a bare declarative doesn't felicitously open with either -- these also double as 2 of this batch's 4 true persona rows (vocative addressee).
posRules.adverbs_chunk_1syllable: 못/잘 (from the brief's 1-syllable list): example anchors the adverb directly against a predicate ('저는 매운 음식을 못 먹어요.' / '저는 잠을 잘 자요.'); cloze answer = adverb+predicate chunk ('못 먹어요' / '잘 자요'); distractors = same adverb + a clashing predicate that is nonsense given the object already stated ('못 자요'/'못 입어요'/'못 타요' after '매운 음식을'; '잘 입어요'/'잘 타요'/'잘 써요' after '잠을').
posRules.adverbs_open_frame: 가장/보통/아주/아직/안녕히/얼마나/열심히/왜/참 (multi-syllable or, for 참, folded to reach the 2-syllable game-contract minimum): example anchors the adverb in a concrete situation; cloze answer = the adverb (or adverb+predicate fold where needed for length); distractors = adverbs of an incompatible class (degree adverbs in a plain-existence/imperative frame, dangling connectives in a self-contained single sentence, etc.) that read as nonsense with that specific predicate.
posRules.pronouns: Deictic/interrogative examples with a real referent. Fold-type pronouns (그/그것/그쪽/이것/이쪽/저것/저쪽/무엇/뭐/어디/언제, plus the bound possessives 내/제 folded to a following noun for the 2-syllable minimum) get answer = pronoun+particle (or pronoun+noun for 내/제, which cannot themselves carry a particle); distractors = a pronoun of a different deictic class (person/thing/place/time) + the same particle, producing a category-violation or particle-form 비문 (e.g. bare demonstratives 그것/무엇/저것 cannot directly precede a noun as a possessive without 의, so '그것 이름은' is ungrammatical) -- judged by reading, recorded in the evidence table.
posRules.dependent_nouns_counters: 가지/권/년/때/마리/명/번/살/쪽/호/중/씨 (+ numeral-determiners 마흔/백만/서른/십만/아흔/여든/일흔 and numerals 구십/팔십/억, which use the identical mechanic): example = numeral (or name, for 씨) + counter matching the noun/referent; cloze answer = numeral+counter chunk (folding in a directly-fused copula 이에요/예요 where the sentence structure requires it, so the copula never sits as a bare alternating particle immediately after the blank); distractors = the SAME leading numeral/name + a WRONG counter that categorically clashes with the noun (e.g. '삼 명이에요'/'삼 권이에요'/'삼 살이에요' for a bus-route number '삼 번이에요') -- deterministic and always nonsense by category mismatch, each distractor independently correct in its OWN particle/copula allomorph. 것 (grammatical, not a numeral classifier) uses 'N은 제 것이에요' with category-mismatch noun distractors instead (제 친구예요/제 나라예요/제 이름이에요). 때 avoids the 2급 '-(으)ㄹ 때' pattern entirely by using the 1급-safe 'N + 때' frame ('시험 때'), never a verb-attributive.
posRules.determiners: 무슨/어떤/여러 (true 관형사, near-synonymous with each other and with the frame's other choices per the brief's own escape hatch: 'ONLY if nonsense else Tier B'): example = determiner + noun; cloze answer = determiner+noun chunk; distractors = a bare dictionary-form verb + the SAME noun (Tier B, e.g. '가다 음식'/'먹다 음식'/'오다 음식'), since a bare infinitive cannot grammatically modify a following noun without proper attributive conjugation (-는/-(으)ㄴ/-(으)ㄹ) -- always 비문, mirroring the PREDICATE_SLOT_WAIVER bare-dictionary-form technique from Batch 25-29's 용언 rows, adapted here to an attributive slot instead of a predicate slot.
posRules.numerals_interjections: 스물 folds to a bare copula predicate ('스물이에요', a wide-open predicate slot exactly like Batch 25's PREDICATE_SLOT_WAIVER noun+이에요 rows) with category-mismatch noun distractors (가방이에요/이름이에요/우산이에요). 구십/팔십/천 (천 added R8, see cheonDecisionNote) use the counter-swap mechanic like the dependent nouns. 그래/아 (interjections) use a preceding-question/apology response frame ('우리 이따 만날까? 그래, 좋아.' / '미안해요! 아, 괜찮아요.') with Tier B bare-dictionary-verb distractors replacing only the interjection token ('가다, 좋아' / '먹다, 좋아' / '오다, 좋아'), mirroring the live precedent for 네/아니요/와 (pos_de=Ausdruck).

personaRowsNote: R8 (2026-09-16): tightened to Fable's 'true speaker with an explicit marker' standard -- a row counts only when the persona is the speaker AND either (a) addressed/named via vocative ('마야 씨, ...', '민호 씨, ...', '레나 씨, ...') or (b) the first-person line unambiguously self-identifies as that persona by canon (내 이름은 준이에요 -- states the speaker's name directly). The first draft's 9 generic '저는...' attributions carried no such marker and are dropped. 4 true persona rows remain, meeting the >=4 floor set for function-word batches (lower than the >=8 used for verb/noun batches, since this batch's content has few natural slots for a named speaker) with each persona used exactly once (well under the <=2 cap).
